# pi-model-sync

> omp (oh my pi) / upstream pi extension: routes subagent models by the spawning session's current model. It covers omp-native subagents and pi-subagent's `subagent` tool. Profiles can be grouped into named presets (one active per config layer). Zero dependencies; the hosts load the TypeScript sources directly. Managed via the `/model-sync` command.

## Install (pick the user's host)

- omp: `omp plugin install npm:@sencha930511/pi-model-sync`
- upstream pi: `pi install npm:@sencha930511/pi-model-sync`
- git, tag-pinned (either host): `omp plugin install git:github.com/SenCha930511/pi-model-sync@v0.5.0` / `pi install git:github.com/SenCha930511/pi-model-sync@v0.5.0`
- omp marketplace: `omp plugin marketplace add SenCha930511/omp-marketplace`, then `omp plugin install pi-model-sync@sencha930511`

Verify after installing: start the host and run `/model-sync list`. It prints the active config layer, the active preset, and that preset's profiles. With no config file yet, it prints the first-run hint instead of an error.

## Minimal config

Global `~/.omp/agent/pi-model-sync.json` (or `~/.pi/agent/pi-model-sync.json` when the `~/.omp` file is absent), project `<repo>/.omp/pi-model-sync.json`; `PI_MODEL_SYNC_CONFIG` overrides the path.

```json
{
  "activePreset": "default",
  "presets": {
    "default": [
      { "main": "provider/main-model", "subagents": { "explore": "provider/child-model", "*": "provider/default" } }
    ]
  }
}
```

`activePreset` picks the preset whose profile list is in effect for that layer; a missing, empty, or null name routes nothing (fail closed, no fallback), and `preset use` repairs the selection. A typo-only root, a non-array `profiles` value, or a malformed preset value is a structural error; invalid profile entries are skipped with a warning. Legacy `{ "profiles": [...] }` files still work as a virtual `default` preset, and the first successful `preset create`/`preset copy` converts them. `main` matches the spawning session's model (`provider/id`, bare id, or `*` glob); per-agent selector via exact key then `*` default; first matching profile in file order wins, and `/model-sync move` changes that order. An agent key with no `*` default is not intercepted. An explicit per-call `model` in a pi-subagent call is never overwritten.

## Commands

- `/model-sync [list]`, `/model-sync show [model] [agent]`, `/model-sync add <main> <model>`, `/model-sync set <main> <agent> <model>`, `/model-sync remove <main> [agent]`, `/model-sync move <main> <top|bottom|up|down>`
- `/model-sync preset list`, `/model-sync preset create <name>`, `/model-sync preset copy <source> <name>`, `/model-sync preset rename <old> <new>`, `/model-sync preset use <name>`, `/model-sync preset remove <name>`
- Writes target the global file; add `--project` to write the project file. When the project file exists, a global write warns that the project layer overrides it. `add`/`set`/`remove`/`move` edit only the active preset; `preset remove` refuses the active preset.
- Typing the command shows argument completion for subcommands, profile `main` values and agent keys (`add`, `set`, `remove`, `move`), and existing preset names (`preset use`, `preset remove`, and the source of `preset copy`/`preset rename`). A typed `--project` flag is preserved and not suggested twice.
